question: Can per-q_a multi-pair aggregation of the s049 cascade pool (Hough omega-vote, cross-t_k consensus, q-space agreement) separate truth-q_a from random?
hypothesis: Even if single hypotheses fail, the collective behaviour of all (truth_q_a, q_b) pairs concentrates around truth-omega in a way random q_a's do not.
narrative_md: Closes path C1 across three structurally distinct variants: Hough omega-voting (top rank only at a near-noise bin), cross-t_k consensus (metric saturates with 778-1099 ties), and q-space agreement (best truth-q_a ranks 2098/141706, top-1000 enrichment 0.0x). Unifying cause: at 17% omega-noise the propagation drift makes truth and random q-positions comparable; naive multi-pair averaging inherits the failure because it can't tell which q_b is truth-adjacent. Only peak-stationarity remains as a Phase-3 candidate. Reads truth-q_a as the discriminator target.
